notes: arduino-mkr-zero is not in the provided catalogue, so it is defined as a new part type with a simplified port list.
The manual text says to plug the MKR Zero into the breadboard, but the image shows it separate and wired with 3 jumpers. I followed the image.
Breadboard positions are read from the image. The DHT22 sits in row a of columns 26-29 (VCC, SDA, NC, GND). The jumpers are in row b, the capacitor in row d, and the resistor in row e.
The capacitor and resistor are drawn with long bendable legs (blue and yellow). I treated them as legs inserted directly into the breadboard, not as extra jumper wires.
The 4.7k pull-up resistor goes between VCC (column 26) and data (column 27). The 100nF capacitor goes between VCC (column 26) and GND (column 29).
The microUSB cable is in the parts list but not drawn. It is attached to the MKR Zero USB port, and its far end is not modelled.
The microSD card is inserted in the MKR Zero SD slot. Its internal pin connections are not modelled.
